svg.title: A 34-year-old woman has taken sertraline for two years. Two days ago tramadol was added for back pain, and she doubled it this morning. She is agitated and drenched in sweat. Ankle clonus is easily induced and her reflexes are brisk, more in the legs. She reports nausea and three loose stools. Temperature 38.6 °C, HR 124, BP 162/96, RR 24.
svg.desc: Clonus and hyperreflexia that are worse in the legs, appearing within hours of a serotonergic dose change, are the Hunter criteria findings that name serotonin syndrome. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is the tempting alternative, but it builds over one to three days after a dopamine blocker and produces rigidity with reduced reflexes, not clonus. Reflex findings and core temperature are what track this syndrome, because hyperthermia from sustained muscle activity is what kills.
